Facsimile Images

Apparatus criticus

  • Text based on photograph ;
  • 1: Manganaro 1977: [Ἀπόλλονι κα]ὶ̣ Νύμ̣[φαις]
  • 2: Manganaro 1977: [τὸν βομὸν] οἰκοδ̣[όμεσε]
  • 3: Manganaro 1977: τελέ[ος]

translation

commentary

Manganaro speculates that the block is part of an altar, at least 3.5m wide, on the basis of his proposed (entirely speculative) restoration of the text. The inventory records the piece as coming from the area of the Great Altar, but no other information is preserved: as inventory no.3, the piece was in the museum at its foundation, but there appears to be no trace of the piece in other documentation (not included in Orsi's initial taccuini in which he recorded most of the initial epigraphic collection, and not seemingly mentioned by Kaibel, nor by the earlier editors such as the Prince of Torremuzza, nor the collection of Cesare Gaetani). The letters are clearly classical or early Hellenistic in form, and monumental, but it remains difficult to say more without further context. There is the very faintest possibility that it is part of the lost text recorded in IG XIV.10, originally reported by Metellus (and which has ΟΙΚΟ in line 2), but this was said to come from the area of the Temple of Zeus Olympios, and the reports do not suggest a text of the size that would have been necessary, so this seems extremely unlikely.

bibliography

  • Manganaro 1977 155-156 ph dr https://biblio.inscriptiones.org/epig10001440
  • 1984 34.0978 https://biblio.inscriptiones.org/epig10000796

Widely spaced, large, wide letters, very neatly and regularly carved with a thin groove. Large omicron, Nu with diagonal fully descending, kappa with near full length arms, epsilon with short middle bar.

Line 1 120 Interlineation line 1 to 2
